title: Relationships & Delete Rules
hints: Set the to-one side (`note.folder`); the inverse to-many updates itself.
Deleting a folder cascades to its notes; deleting a note nullifies its folder link.
jsBridge: Relationships with inverses and delete rules (cascade/nullify) are foreign keys with `ON DELETE CASCADE` / `SET NULL`. Core Data keeps both sides of the object graph in sync in memory, where SQL only enforces them on the database.

compass.q: An ORM relation with `onDelete: 'cascade'` vs Core Data's cascade rule: where does each run (DB vs object graph)?
Why does Core Data warn when a relationship has no inverse? What goes wrong?
Cascade vs nullify vs deny: which fits folder → notes, and which fits note → tags?
A to-many relationship is an unordered `NSSet` by default. How do you keep notes in a user-defined order?
